subject: Redwood POC - Observability & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finmaps.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finmaps.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood POC - Observability & Success Criteria

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. This thread is a short recap + proposed next steps so we can move to a 4-week POC focused on inference economics and observability. Please confirm and flag anything missing.

Scope we discussed
- Surface-level integration: point Redwood API at a staging model (no production traffic)
- Objective: validate latency/throughput, per-token cost, and end-to-end observability/export to your telemetry stack
- Duration: 4 weeks (target kickoff: 2026-03-08)

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or adjust)
1) Latency: 95th percentile for single-turn generation < 200 ms for target prompt mix
2) Cost: effective cost-per-inference <= $0.02 averaged over test workload
3) Reliability: error rate < 0.1% measured as 5xx/failed responses
4) Throughput: sustain 50 req/s for 30 minutes without SLA degradation
5) Observability: ability to export traces and token-level cost breakdown to your Grafana/Splunk and have dashboarding for the above metrics

Observability/POC plan (high level)
- Dashboards: POC Overview, Latency Breakdown, Token Cost, Error Rates, Traces Summary
- Tracing: distributed traces with 100% sampling during POC window; root cause drill-down for tail latency
- Logs: redwood runtime logs exported to S3 and optional syslog/Splunk forwarder (we can enable retention 30d/90d)
- Metrics: request_rate, tokens_generated, token_cost_per_model, latency_p50/p90/p95, error_count, cache_hit_rate
- Alerts: p95 latency > 250ms (warning), error_rate > 0.5% (critical), token_cost deviates +/-20% vs baseline
- Ownership: Redwood: runtime instrumentation + dashboard templates; FinMaps: provisioning Splunk/Grafana endpoint and sample traffic

Next steps
1) You confirm success criteria and the timeline (kickoff 2026-03-08)
2) I’ll send a short POC runbook and an observability playbook (attached) and loop in Rishi + Vivek for technical setup
3) Set a 30-min kickoff to align test datasets and access (I can do 2026-03-08 morning PT)

Attachments: FinMaps_POC_Runbook.pdf (runbook), observability_playbook.pdf (dashboards + metrics spec)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Alex — appreciated. Quick clarifications in-line and attached the runbook + playbook per our plan. Highlights:

- Latency: we can make the target conditional on prompt-length buckets. Updated success criteria in attached runbook: for median prompt (~120 tokens) p95 <= 250ms; for short prompts (<40 tokens) p95 <= 200ms.
- Batching/caching assumptions (from Redwood): continuous batching enabled up to 64 tokens per batch; KV prefix caching enabled for repeated prefixes; default sampling has token-level cost attribution enabled in the playbook. We documented recommended batch_size and cache policies in the runbook.
- Tracing: Redwood supports OTLP and can forward spans to your collector. For the POC we recommend 100% sampling (at least during baseline runs) and we’ll include trace_id in the exported spans so you can correlate in Grafana/Splunk.

Detailed POC plan (summary)
Week 0 (pre-kickoff)
- FinMaps: provide sample request corpus (CSV or JSONL), Grafana/Splunk collector endpoints, and any allowlisted IPs
- Redwood: provision staging model endpoint, share credentials and test endpoint, import dashboard templates

Week 1 (baseline + trace)
- Run baseline traffic at 10 req/s with 100% tracing; validate trace export and dashboard wiring
Week 2 (scale & latency)
- Ramp to target throughput (50 req/s), validate p95 latency and error-rate thresholds
Week 3 (cost optimization)
- Enable caching/quantization recommendations and measure cost delta; compare token-cost metrics
Week 4 (final validation + handoff)
- Run end-to-end validation, export final report, discuss handoff/next steps

Success criteria (updated)
- p95 latency: <=250ms for median prompt (120 tokens)
- token_cost: average <= $0.02 after enabling optimizations (Week 3)
- error_rate: <0.1% under load
- traces: OTLP export verified with trace_id correlation in Grafana/Splunk

Attachments: FinMaps_POC_Runbook.pdf, observability_playbook.pdf

Can we lock a 30-min kickoff on 2026-03-08 at 10:00 PT? If that works I’ll send an invite and pre-kickoff checklist.

Thanks — cc’ing Rishi and Vivek for technical setup/questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Redwood POC - Observability & Success Criteria (technical notes)

Hi team — quick technical notes ahead of kickoff:
- Traffic profile: please share a sample of 500-1000 requests that reflect your mix (we need prompt lengths + frequency distribution). Ranges matter for batching behavior.
- KV cache: if you expect repeated prefixes (autocomplete), enable prefix caching; we’ll provide recommended TTLs in test-config.yaml (attached).
- Quantization: to hit the cost targets, we’ll test a 4-bit quantized variant in Week 3; we’ll keep a non-quantized control for quality checks.
- Tracing: OTLP/collector endpoint is preferred. If you can’t accept incoming connections, we can push to S3 and your collector can pull. For the POC we recommend 100% sampling for the first 72 hours, then drop to 10% for steady-state metrics.
- Log export: Redwood runtime supports S3 export (parquet+json) and a syslog/Splunk forwarder. If you want near-real-time logs in Splunk, enable the forwarder with TLS and token auth.

I attached test-config.yaml with recommended params (batch_size: 64, trace_sample_rate: 1.0 for baseline, cache_ttl_seconds: 300). Let me know if you need a different default.

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
